speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So, anti-gravity is Google's agentic coding product for technical and non-technical users.

text: We launched back in November of 2025 and have been accelerating devs both within Google and externally ever since.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So, let's talk a little bit more about what anti-gravity is.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: We have and always will be unapologetically agent first.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So we debuted the anti-gravity IDE last year with a brand new agent manager concept.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And it was a platform to manage and orchestrate many agents.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: As you can see, not only is it your own dedicated mission control for your agents and projects, you have sub-agents, you have all the new models, you have work trees, scheduled tasks, voice mode, there are so many things to unpack with the product.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: But I don't want to spend today telling you about the product, I want to tell you a little bit more about the behind the scenes, some of the principles that went into it, and notably, some of the things that led to its roadmap.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So as some of you, for the long-time AI Eng fans, this is actually my fifth time speaking at AI Eng, and I've been building developer's tools since 2022.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And the one thing that has stood above all other lessons that I've talked about is the idea of scaling with intelligence.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: This means that as the model gets better, so should your product.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And the frontier edge of whatever model you are serving should be apparent inside of your user's product experience.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So let's get into more concrete examples of what this means.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So for those of you that follow me on X or hear me just yap generally for the last four years, you'll know that I've been working on a number of these sort of transformations year over year over year.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: In 2022, I was working on autocomplete and chat sidebars.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: This was based on embeddings, rules files, AST syntax tree parsing, basically everything inside of that app is deterministic, because that's all that the model could really handle.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And in 2024, when agents came onto the scene, it completely changed how developers were going to do work.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: With it came new primitives, like MCPs, custom tools, and permission systems.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And with 2025, we introduced Antigravity's Agent Manager with many other products following suit in that similar form factor, with users managing many agents at once in parallel.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And this led to things like skills, hooks, artifacts, and a couple other primitives, and that sort of defined the 2025 era.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So let's talk a little bit about 2026 and what those primitives might be.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Before we answer this question, I want to take you back to some of these battle scars that are a little bit closer to home.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Scaling with intelligence really is not easy.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: It's really hard to take away something that users love and are familiar with to lead them down potentially, and that's a big keyword, a better path.

text: We aren't right 100% of the time, but there are two that jumped to mind when I was putting together the slides for this talk.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: The first one is giving AI a terminal.

text: We all remember fears about son of Anton deleting your entire codebase and doing catastrophic things to both your startup, your company, et cetera, et cetera.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: But as models got better and people invested in primitives, such as permission systems, users ended up building faster, they ended up shipping more, and they did so safely.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So we were able to overcome this, and as models got smarter, they were able to make better decisions about what they should and should not run in your terminal.

text: The second instance is this tweet, which is very representative of sort of the yelling that I got when we removed chat from Windsurf.

text: So a lot of users were yelling at our team because we took away something that was very dear to them, the chat sidebar, and replaced it with only an agent.

text: But when we look back, models have advanced.

text: So we decoupled the agent manager from the IDE, and with antigravity 2.0, we split them into separate applications.

speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And our prediction is that this idea of agent orchestration, you can call it agent teams, you can call it swarms, you can call it software factories, is the future, and we're willing to bet on that future.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: So here are the primitives for what we're calling the agent teams 2026 era.

text: And so as you can see with this particular example, sub-agent primitives are one of the defining parts about building a 2026 era of agent teams.

text: Now, traditionally, this was a lot of Jupyter Notebook elbow grease, essentially, but when you start working with the new primitives in 2026, you end up with a lot cleaner of a workflow.
